items.content: Opening shot outdoors (chapter title: 'Just the Tree of Us'). Amit: 'It is because we are decluttering. We have done away with the…
Amit on monkish renunciation: when monks preached a sparse life, 'they did not have a Kindle. They did not have a Fender Strat. Easy for…
Ajay offers the minimalist motto 'He who dies with the least toys wins.' Amit adds: 'but it also matters where you start.'
Amit, connoisseur of thirteen shower gels: 'I know as much about shower gels as you know about Ukraine.'
Amit on Harford's book: 'Messy, by the way, is M-E-S-S-Y, not the footballer.'
Amit citing Marvin Gaye's 'Wherever I Lay My Hat, that's my home': 'Except that whenever I've had a hat, I've lost it. Which is profound.'
Amit interrupts Ajay's account of 1991-era scarcity: one thing that was abundant then but scarce now is 'the days of our youth.' The…
Ajay dreams of writing symphonies in solitary confinement, like his heroes who wrote poetry in concentration camps. Amit: 'I hope you're…
Ajay: 'before you find your prince, you've got to kiss a hundred frogs.' Amit: 'Why you giggle like that? Have you ever kissed a frog?'
Ajay (noting his own contribution to the show is only 30%) asks how Amit ships two shows every week. Amit: 'Badly.'
Amit mimes running in his chair ('this is very Bengali of me'). Ajay: 'The rarest object in the world, a Bengali sprinter.' Amit:…
Before Ajay's book pick, Amit warns: 'This episode is about decluttering. You're not allowed to buy what he recommends right now.' Ajay:…
Amit's Erich Fromm joke: Fromm meets a rotund Bengali in a Kolkata market (Bengalis like talking to foreigners, 'it makes them feel…
Amit, promising Ken Liu's story will make Ajay cry: 'So when we record our next episode, gentle reader, Ajay's eyes will be red.'
Chuck Palahniuk's 'the things you own end up owning you', Amit's thesis for the episode.
Annie Dillard: 'How we live our days is how we live our lives.'
Tsundoku, the condition of owning more books than you read, which Amit happily confesses to.
Tim Harford, introduced by Amit as 'also a fellow two-time winner of the Bastiat Prize'.
Vera Brandes, 17, organised the Köln Concert. Amit notes she was 'even younger than our very own Nomsita', the show's 19-year-old editor.
'Above the API' versus 'below the API', a phrase Ajay introduced to Amit, used for people who direct their own creative work rather than…
Amit: 'I'm not gonna go all Marie Kondo and say, no, only have thirty things.'
Bob Dylan, 'Every Grain of Sand', read aloud by Amit: 'I am hanging in the balance of a perfect finished plan, like every sparrow…
Sturgeon's Law (most of everything is crap) and Tyler Cowen's rule of never gifting a book you didn't like.
Ajay on fashion: some of it is genuine creativity, 'it's not only a case of three dollar wine.'
Pink Floyd's 'Time' from Dark Side of the Moon: 'plans that either come to naught or half a page of scribbled lines.' Ajay: 'I have lots…
Steve Jobs to Jony Ive after returning to Apple in the 1990s: learn to say no to things that you love.
